title: Customer-supplied parts
purpose: Staff rules for fitting parts the customer brings.
facts: Three things said before taking the keys: normal labour rate, no warranty, labour charged again if the part is wrong.
The part goes on the order as a hand-typed line with "customer supplied", price 0.00, no part number (the one legitimate hand-typed part line; ERP mess kind 7).
Order note "Customer-supplied part: no warranty" prints on the invoice.
Refused items as on the public page; exceptions only through slot 4 or 22.
No company account supplies its own parts.

list_items.item: Say the three things before taking the keys: normal labour rate, no warranty on part or labour, and if the part is wrong the labour is charged again. Get a yes.
On the order, type the part on its own line with "customer supplied" in the description, price $0.00. It will have no part number. That is the one case where a hand-typed part line is right.
Write "Customer-supplied part: no warranty" in the order notes. It prints on the invoice.
We do not fit customer-supplied brake hydraulic parts, airbag or seat-belt parts, or tires over six years old. No exceptions at the counter; send the customer to Greg or Dale if they want to argue.
Shop supplies apply as on any hourly job.
